claims.confidence: high (that the code is still unconfirmed)
claims.surfaces_universe: tracked *.html at a8072e12, literal 'TBC (Cheryl)' (re-measured this pass)
claims.assessment: The pupil-facing wording is honest: it marks the code unconfirmed, names its owner, and frames UAS as recording rather than qualification. Two residual risks, both narrow. (1) A witness sheet can be printed and filed with a blank unit code. (2) PEQ-YEAR-1 set this row's status from the REGISTRATION fact, which made a claim about an unread unit CODE read as centre-confirmed; corrected here. Registration and unit entry are settled; the code is not, and the two must not be collapsed.

claims.hold: 25 of these files (Build 5 / Grow 5 / Launch 15) are HELD BYTE-PRISTINE by Matt's restore-sitting ruling, _close/OPEN_ITEMS.md item 17: 'Until that sitting all 25 sheets stay byte-pristine'. No pass may edit them, including to improve the qualifier. The remaining 38 surfaces (v3_40min variants and .body.txt copies) carry the IDENTICAL hidden comment, are outside that ruling's set, and were unaccounted for in every record until this pass measured them. They are reported, not edited: editing them alone would diverge the variants from the sheets they mirror while the hold stands.
claims.canonical_wording: Every AQA UAS unit code and unit title on any estate surface is an UNVERIFIED CENTRE RECORD AWAITING CONFIRMATION from the UAS coordinator's entry record. It is not a compliance claim, and no surface may present it as one. Registration and unit entry being settled does not confirm a code.
